desc:
A binary tree is full if every node has either zero or two children. You are given the preorder traversal (node, left, right) and the postorder traversal (left, right, node) of a full binary tree with distinct node values. Rebuild the tree and return it in level-order encoding.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed (or returned) as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree below: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For preorder = [1, 2, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7] and postorder = [4, 5, 2, 6, 7, 3, 1] the answer is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]. For preorder = [8] and postorder = [8] the answer is [8].

For general trees preorder and postorder do not determine the tree (a lone child may be left or right), but for full trees they do, so the answer is unique. The empty tree has empty arrays and the answer [].
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 1,499 and n is odd or zero
postorder is a permutation of preorder, and both come from the same full binary tree
hints: The first preorder entry is the root and the last postorder entry is the root. What is the second preorder entry, if the tree has more than one node?
In a full tree the root has two children, so preorder[1] is the root of the left subtree. Find it in the postorder array: that subtree ends exactly there.

If the left subtree's root is at postorder index j (and the current range starts at index q), the left subtree has j - q + 1 nodes. Split both arrays by that size and recurse on the two parts, using a value-to-postorder-index map.
editorial: Preorder starts with the root followed by the left subtree and then the right subtree. Postorder lists the left subtree, then the right subtree, then the root. If the tree is full and has more than one node, the root has two children, and preorder[1] is the root of the left subtree. In the postorder array the root of a subtree is its last entry, so the left subtree occupies everything from the start of the range up to the position of preorder[1]. That gives its size, hence also the boundary between the subtrees in both arrays.

Fullness is what makes the split unique. If a node could have a single child, preorder[1] could be the root of a left or of a right subtree and the position in the postorder array would not tell which. Using a dictionary from value to postorder index, every split costs O(1), and the whole reconstruction is O(n). The reference solution processes ranges with an explicit stack to be safe on deep trees.
